identity.matching: The independent positive of the password-bytes family (287, CVE-2025-22228's 72-byte limit): the shared concern is the password's UTF-8 representation, characters against bytes. This pair adds no length restriction of its own, and encoding preservation is no authentication policy. Only the BCrypt.hashpw(String,String) entry is selected: the three-file patch also changes the cached charset in crypto.codec.Utf8 and a test utility.

after.checked: 2026-11-14: fetched by SHA from github.com; one parent, fb39d9c2 (not a merge); author Lars Grefer, 2019-08-09 00:39:09 +0200 (2019-08-08 in UTC), 'StandardCharsets can be used'; three files.

mutant.description: hashpw(String, String) encodes the password with US-ASCII instead of UTF-8, so every non-ASCII character becomes '?' and different non-ASCII passwords of one length hash alike. It breaks preservation at the non-ASCII probes and keeps the ASCII ones.

unresolved: No Maven Central artifact has exactly either side's BCrypt.java: before's equals 5.2.0.M4's (a milestone, published only to repo.spring.io), and 5.2.0.RELEASE's differs from after's by a removed unused import and a `final` dropped from the private method encipher (sources.lock.json).

notes: Concrete controls only: each revision's original BCrypt class in its own JVM, on JDK 21 and 25, over replay/probes.json's 45 probes: three valid salts from upstream's BCryptTests (the 'abc' test vector's cost-6 salt, its stored hash, and the '$2$05$' salt), never a random one, with passwords empty, ASCII, BMP non-ASCII, supplementary, 71, 72 and 73 UTF-8 bytes (in ASCII and in 2-, 3- and 4-byte characters, and with a character straddling byte 72), isolated and reversed surrogates, and null; and four invalid salts from the same tests. Observed: the returned String, or the exception's class. controls/oracle.py checks each side's lines against its statement and the two sides against each other.

On the frozen password and salt domain and the pinned JDK's charset behaviour, both revisions return the same string and throw the same exceptions. No allowed-change region. A proof may reuse a checked summary of the unchanged callee hashpw(byte[],String), bound to its actual bytecode; without that reuse this task stays unresolved beside a separate local conversion lemma, and no cipher is substituted.

The mutation control's concrete side: after and the constructed mutant (after's sources with controls/us-ascii.patch applied, built by after's recipe), each in its own JVM on JDK 21 and 25, with replay's driver, probes and oracle. Expected: after holds, and the mutant fails at the non-ASCII probes.

The mutation control: preservation's claim, its file and domain unchanged, over the mutation pair, after against the constructed mutant. Expected refuted, at the non-ASCII probes. Sensitivity evidence for the preservation claim, never a historical result.

blockers.summary: Predicted from the build files and from HEAD requests to the repositories on 2026-11-14, not from a build. The buildscript's classpath is io.spring.gradle:spring-build-conventions:0.0.23.RELEASE, the Boot 2.2.0.M3 Gradle plugin and nohttp-gradle 0.0.2.RELEASE, with their transitive closure, and Gradle resolves all of it before compiling anything. Decision 1's two extensions (the user, 2026-11-14) allow services.gradle.org, plugins.gradle.org, repo.spring.io and maven.aliyun.com/repository/spring-plugin/ for P3's four Spring plugins (spring-build-conventions, docbook-reference-plugin 0.3.1, propdeps-plugin 0.0.10.RELEASE and spring-io-plugin 0.0.8.RELEASE, each on the mirror, sha1 agreeing, sha256 in sources.lock.json). The rest of the closure is still not reachable. (1) plugins.gradle.org serves every plugin it hosts (gretty 2.2.0, build-info-extractor-gradle 4.7.5, gradle-versions-plugin 0.17.0, asciidoctor-gradle-plugin 1.5.8.1, gradle-ssh-plugin 2.9.0, nohttp-gradle) by a 303 redirect to plugins-artifacts.gradle.org, a host runtime_maven.py neither allows nor follows. (2) At least two second-level dependencies were published only to JCenter, which now redirects to Maven Central, where they 404: org.gretty:gretty-core:2.2.0 (gretty's) and org.jfrog.buildinfo:build-info-extractor:2.11.3 (build-info-extractor-gradle's). They answer 404 on repo.spring.io/milestone and the spring-plugin mirror, and 401 on repo.spring.io's plugins-release and libs-release. They answer 200 on maven.aliyun.com's jcenter, public and gradle-plugin repositories, which the user's decision doesn't cover. The closure wasn't enumerated further, so more such modules may exist. So the upstream build is predicted to fail at its buildscript, and runtime's Gradle route (runtime_upstream.py) wasn't built. Its pins (the 5.5.1 distribution's sha256 from gradle.org's checksum page, and the four plugins) are in sources.lock.json for when it is. The alternative is the extracted-source slice: each commit's BCrypt.java, which needs only the JDK, compiled alone. A hand compile of before's by javac 1.8.0_512 with -g -source 1.8 -target 1.8 gives a BCrypt.class byte-identical to Spring Security 5.2.0.M4's published one (sources.lock.json).

Predicted from a static scan, not from an attempt: jvmcontract gaps on BCrypt.hashpw(String,String) refuses the changed operation itself on both sides, before's String.getBytes(String) and after's String.getBytes(Charset) (an array result of a JDK instance method) and after's read of StandardCharsets.UTF_8 (a JDK static field that is not a compile-time constant); the unchanged callee adds the refused Arrays.copyOf(byte[],int) and Integer.parseInt and StringBuilder.charAt with no approximation. So the strict preservation attempt is predicted to stop at the UTF-16 to UTF-8 conversion, the password-bytes family's shared demand, before the cipher. Run by hand with a binary one lib/src commit old, on classes compiled from each commit's BCrypt.java outside the upstream build (records/hashpw-gaps.json, a note).

Predicted from lib/README.md: the checker takes a String parameter of a regression check as bounded UTF-16 with content, never null, but the claim's domain has a null password (NullPointerException) and a null salt (claims/hashpw-preservation.json); an attempt that can't take them is that refusal, and the claim stays unresolved, never re-read as the non-null domain. The salt domain is seven fixed strings, stated as an assume expression with String.equals.

Before's class is checked against that published class byte for byte, and the slice is labelled as its own scope. It reuses the slice route 305 gets. Then runtime's preparation of both revisions, the replay task (the driver on each revision's crypto classes in its own JVM, on JDK 21 and 25, read by controls/oracle.py), and the mutant: us-ascii.patch applied to after's BCrypt.java and its class compiled into a copy of after's artifact, replayed against the same oracle (it must fail on non-ASCII passwords and only there). The native attempt is queued only after the replay, and its predicted refusals recorded as observed or withdrawn. A conversion lemma bound to the unchanged callee's bytecode is a separate, narrower claim if it is wanted.
